source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-9, HMC-7 and M.2
source_snapshot.procedure: From BMC run `i2cdetect -y -q 8` and `i2ctransfer -y 8 w2@0x6a 0x00 0xd5 r6`; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Generic evidence/photo and unexpected-log checks only; no meaning for HMC-7,0x6a, register0x00d5, M.2 slot or six-byte reply.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; invents physical probing/soldering despite a specific remote sideband transaction.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/CHANGED; treats M.2 seating/handling as core even though the source specifies no removal/reseat, while leaving the sideband target/decoder unresolved.
source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Test connections between BMC I2C-9, HMC-7 and M.2
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2cdetect -y -q 8 i2ctransfer -y 8 w2@0x6a 0x00 0xd5 r6
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: NO | -- not runnable by agent: testing the physical I2C connection/link between the named components (BMC I2C-9, HMC-7 and M.2) is a hardware-integrity check that requires probing/soldering the actual I2C traces and collecting photos per the criteria; the agent cannot touch the hardware or take photos over SSH.

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-9, HMC-7 and M.2 — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify the BMC I2C-9 management path through the named HMC-7 element reaches the intended M.2 sideband endpoint and returns a valid device-specific register response.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-9 to Linux bus8 through the exact HMC-7 element to an M.2 slot
Definition of HMC-7 naming and whether it is controller/channel/mux/bridge
Identity of address0x6a and proof it belongs to the intended installed M.2 endpoint
Vendor definition for register0x00d5, write-pointer safety and six returned bytes
M.2 slot/BDF/serial/model/firmware correlation and sideband-versus-PCIe identity
Bus owner/driver, timeout/NACK/error criteria and BMC/HMC/M.2 recovery
test_case.test_command: Map BMC I2C-9 to Linux bus8; clarify HMC-7 identity/function and its route to a specific M.2 slot; identify0x6a/register0x00d5 protocol; capture owner and device-health baseline; avoid broad scan; run one bounded combined read; decode six bytes and correlate them with M.2 serial/slot/sideband identity and controller error status without changing storage or physical seating.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

Confirm no physical probing/reseat is required unless separately scoped.
safety_gate: Do not run broad quick-write discovery; query only the approved0x6a endpoint
Confirm the two-byte pointer is non-mutating for the exact sideband device
Coordinate with BMC/HMC driver ownership and avoid concurrent raw access
Do not remove/reseat M.2, alter PCIe/storage state or write sideband registers
Perform one bounded read; abort on identity mismatch, invalid length/value, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or storage/management health regression
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-9/bus8/HMC-7/M.2 sideband path
BMC/HMC identities and exact M.2 slot/BDF/serial/model/firmware mapping
Owner/driver state and pre-read storage/management health
Vendor register0x00d5 definition and expected six-byte matrix
Timestamped exact transfer with stdout/stderr, exit code, latency, raw and decoded bytes
Pre/post BMC/HMC/sideband/storage error logs, unchanged device availability and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy requires BMC controller/bus, target address, management path, vendor protocol and expected reply. Storage device identity must be immutable and must not be inferred from index alone.

source_conflict.reason: The source does not define HMC-7, map logical I2C-9 to bus8, identify0x6a/register0x00d5 or provide expected six bytes/M.2 slot identity. Prior reviews additionally invent physical probing and M.2 handling.
